content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.4) — model is overly conservative, often missing downward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model fails to adjust downward quickly; delay in price correction by 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices too far from recent mean; true price tends to revert toward 75–82 range after 10–14 days.
- Overshoot after spikes: model often peaks 2–3 days after a price spike, then drops sharply — true price usually peaks earlier and declines more gradually.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — model overweights momentum.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is > -0.3, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for each day of negative sentiment accumulation.
- Avoid “overfitting to recent highs”: model often assumes recent high is sustainable — true price usually corrects within 7–10 days if sentiment turns negative.
